title: Disparities in Peer Review Tone and the Role of Reviewer Anonymity

bias_targets.methodology: Analyzing peer review sentiment (using a fine-tuned SciBERT model), evaluative n-gram frequencies, and tone classifications (using GPT-4o) across male and female corresponding authors.
Comparing reviewer sentiment, language patterns, and LLM-classified review tones across white and non-white corresponding authors.
Measuring differences in peer review sentiment, evaluative n-grams, and review tones directed at authors with Western versus Eastern institutional affiliations.
Evaluating the effect of an author's institutional affiliation rank (Top 100 versus other institutions) on the sentiment, linguistic structure, and tone of peer review feedback.
Using regression models and career stage binning (early, mid, senior) to assess how an author's academic age (years since first publication) impacts the tone and sentiment of received reviews.
